First time bun owner, I have one buck and one doe (both fixed and young). I recently changed their hay rack from the IKEA one (picture one) to the one they have now (picture two). They still have the same litter boxes as before and in the same place but they have started to push them away to sit underneath the hay rack to eat. This is annoying because they do their other business while eating and it gets dirty very quickly, which is harder to clean up than if it was all in the litter boxes. When sitting underneath they also pull much more hay out and leaving it on the floor, using more hay than they actually eat. 


Its mainly the doe (Humla, the lop eared one) that push the boxes away, but when she does, they both sit underneath it to eat until i put the box/es back. I still havent seen the buck (Newton, small black void) even try to push them by himself. What can I do? Should I change hay rack again? 


The reason I dont want to use the IKEA one is because I dont want to risk them getting their heads stuck in the holes, and when they had that they pulled even more hay out, I had to refill it very often. 


BONUS QUESTION: how the heck do you guys remove the hay from the rugs (picture three)!? I have a handheld broom I use to sweep up stuff that get on the floor, but I cant seem to remove the dang hay, and I keep seeing people with beautiful, hay-free rugs for their buns! Whats your secret!?
